newsitem.title: CHINA: HK property stocks up on steady interest rate hope.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks up on steady interest rate hope.

text.p: Shares of Hong Kong property stocks rose on buying fueled by expectations of steady interest rates and hopes that local property prices are bottoming out soon, brokers said on Wednesday.

"Anticipation of steady U.S. rates and the high U.S. stock market close, plus signs of a bottoming out of the property market are seen boosted buying interest," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
Shares of Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd rose HK$1.75 or 1.98 percent to HK$90 in late morning.
New World Development Co Ltd rose HK$0.80 or 1.67 percent to HK$48.80, Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd rose HK$0.75 to HK$74.25 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rose HK$0.50 to HK$67.00.

The Dow industrials surged 154.93 points, or 1.96 percent, to a record 8,061.65 on Tuesday following comments made by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, who suggested that a rise in interest rates might not happen anytime soon.
Brokers said the interest rate environment should help the property sector, which has been under pressure due to government plans to curb rising real estate prices.

"Anticipation that the government is unlikely to impose further measures to curb property speculation in the near run following a recent correction in property prices aided demand, said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.

"Investors may focus on the real value of the property counter in view of a limited downside for property prices," Li said. "Their (property developers') profit margins are still high because their land banks are relatively cheap in cost."
Vickers' Mak said that while property stocks had firmed up a bit, the sector was unlikely to outperform the market in the short run when the overall market rally was still led by a few stocks.
